records.note: In project p-co (Checkout Redesign) and updatedById is u-leo (Leo Park). The only other doc in p-co (d-22) was last updated by Sam, so d-21 is the unique doc in the project last edited by Leo. Clean match.
In project p-co, but updatedById is u-sam, not u-leo. Leo Park is only the creator (creatorId), so 'last edited' fails even though he authored it originally.

No projectId at all; it is attached to the Commerce initiative (initiativeId in-com), which merely contains project p-co. Being linked to an initiative that includes the project is not the same as being 'in the Checkout Redesign project.' Title ('Commerce QA overview') also gives no indication of belonging to Checkout Redesign.

projectId is p-co2, whose name is 'Checkout Redesign v2' — a distinct, separate project from 'Checkout Redesign' (different id, name has an explicit v2 suffix). A careless reader might be drawn in by the shared 'Checkout Redesign' prefix, but a careful reader treats it as a different project, so this fails r1.
projectId is p-pay (Payments Revamp), an unrelated project. Title and project both clearly don't match Checkout Redesign.

structured_output.differences: The conditions match my step-1 reading closely. r4 (uniqueness) is largely a restatement/consequence of r2 rather than an independent constraint, but it doesn't change the outcome. No condition was missing or extraneous relative to the plain request.

ambiguity_effects.phrase: the doc Leo Park last edited (project scope for 'last' vs. as a locating filter)
ambiguity_effects.explain: In principle one could ask whether 'last edited by Leo' is computed globally then checked against the project, or computed only among the project's docs. Given the actual data, both approaches land on d-21: within p-co, only d-21 was last touched by Leo (d-22 was last touched by Sam), so scoping order doesn't change the outcome. Not a live ambiguity here.

ambiguity_effects.phrase: 'last edited' (edit event vs. last editor of the doc)
ambiguity_effects.explain: Both phrasings describe the same underlying fact captured by updatedById. A careful reader reads 'the doc Leo Park last edited' as 'the doc whose most recent edit was made by Leo Park,' which is exactly what updatedById encodes. No split in outcome.

ambiguity_effects.phrase: 'in the Checkout Redesign project' modifying 'the doc' vs. modifying 'last edited'
ambiguity_effects.explain: Standard English parsing attaches the prepositional phrase to 'the doc' (the doc's location), not to the verb phrase. A careful reader would not seriously entertain the second reading, and even if they did, it produces the same restriction to project p-co docs before checking Leo's edits.

structured_output.naturalness_note: The request reads like an ordinary, realistic instruction a Linear user would give a colleague or assistant — identifying a doc by last-editor and project rather than by ID, and asking for a straightforward rename. Nothing about the phrasing signals it was constructed for a test."
